{"type":"step_start","timestamp":1794693637293,"sessionID":"ses_e23eecc5affeVovNaW1r8zex49","part":{"id":"prt_1dc13a49d001B0OcWtx1Ry5N1D","messageID":"msg_1dc1385200010fMfwdAE4Htnq5","sessionID":"ses_e23eecc5affeVovNaW1r8zex49","snapshot":"","type":"step-start"}}
{"type":"text","timestamp":1794693639507,"sessionID":"ses_e23eecc5affeVovNaW1r8zex49","part":{"id":"prt_1dc13a49f001a7S6I9Q6TpiAjh","messageID":"msg_1dc1385200010fMfwdAE4Htnq5","sessionID":"ses_e23eecc5affeVovNaW1r8zex49","type":"text","text":"I've ended the shift, and all four customer-facing services were at 0% errors for the last 22 minutes (from minute 98 to 120). There were three faults, and two of them left a retry storm that only cleared once I temporarily rejected a share of requests (\"throttled\"). Callers aren't told to retry rejected requests, so that lets the backlog drain.\n\n**1. payments-db lost its primary node (started 23 minutes before the page).** This broke web-storefront (about 99% of requests failing) and admin-portal (about 27%).\n- I switched payments-db over to its standby node at minute 9.\n- Callers' retries kept payments-db overloaded, so I throttled it to 50% for about 10 minutes and the backlog cleared.\n- import-svc, which web-storefront depends on, was also stuck overloaded. When I lifted its first throttle, it overloaded again: its traffic is now about 4,700 requests/min, against about 1,800 before the incident and about 2,800 its 8 replicas can handle. I scaled it to 16 replicas and throttled it briefly. web-storefront was clean by minute 59.\n\n**2. A risk-svc deploy (v78) broke TLS connections from inventory-svc (started 22 minutes before the page).** v78 raised the minimum TLS version from 1.2 to 1.3. partner-api showed a steady 4.3% error rate, which never crossed the alert threshold. It was still the most expensive fault, at about $780/min.\n- risk-svc was at 88% CPU. A rollback fails 30% of requests while it runs, and the retries could have overloaded it. So I scaled it to 6 replicas first, then rolled back v78.\n- partner-api was at 0% errors by minute 43, and I set risk-svc back to its normal 3 replicas.\n\n**3. A new fault began during the shift: a notifications-svc deploy (v24) at minute 75.** It hardcoded the database connection pool to 4 connections. web-storefront errors went back up to about 91% through ranking-svc.\n- I rolled back v24 at minute 90 and throttled notifications-svc to 70% to clear the retry storm. I lifted the throttle at minute 96, and web-storefront was back to 0% by minute 98.\n\n**Things left as they are:**\n- **import-svc is still at 16 replicas** instead of its normal 8. That costs $24/min, about $1,600 for the shift. I kept it because its traffic was still 2.6 times what it was before the incident, and it was running at 85% CPU even at 16. The next shift should decide whether the extra traffic is real and whether to keep the replicas.\n- **limits-svc has had a CPU alert since before the page** (98% at minute 59). It isn't on any path a customer request uses, so I left it alone.\n- **I didn't touch two other changes I looked at:** an inventory-svc rate-limit change and a notifications-svc credential rotation. Their diffs had nothing to do with the errors.","time":{"start":1794693637279,"end":1794693639505}}}
